articles.title: Pebble Grain
articles.summary: Large rounded dimples like leather pebble grain; broad roughness bumps, no colour shift, low contrast. Reads as a smooth sheen with a faint dimpled or beaded feel in the highlight; the bumps vanish with distance.
articles.what: Adds large rounded roughness bumps like leather pebble grain — dimpled surface texture variation Up close: A soft honeycomb of rounded bumps, about 15 px, in staggered rows with slightly lighter tops and darker joins. On satin it is nearly invisible; on metallic it makes a gentle dimpled beading across the bright band. From a distance: Reads as a smooth sheen with a faint dimpled or beaded feel in the highlight; the bumps vanish with distance. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Surface & Spray Texture (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Surface & Spray Texture", or search for "Pebble Grain".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: wide metallic panels show it best
Skip satin base: little effect
Low contrast; numbers read fine.
Almost invisible, a faint dimple in the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not a leather colour: no tan or brown tint, shine only
Not orange peel film: soft low bumps, not bright-rimmed bubbles
Avoid: may look dirty on gloss, too subtle at distance.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Pebble Grain over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Anodized Texture
articles.summary: Fine nanoporous anodized texture with a subtle hexagonal pore grid and moderate metallic sheen. Reads as a clean, even anodised-aluminium satin with no visible pattern; only the quality of the sheen changes.
articles.what: Anodized aluminum nanoporous oxide layer — hexagonal three-cosine pore grid (100+ pores/unit), high metallic oxide inter-pore matrix, low metallic pore centers, moderate Up close: Nearly smooth: a smooth sheen broken by a very fine pore grain, only a few faint dotted specks and hairline wiggles show inside the highlight, with no visible shapes. The hex pore grid is finer than the pixels can show at 1:1. From a distance: Reads as a clean, even anodised-aluminium satin with no visible pattern; only the quality of the sheen changes. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Surface & Spray Texture (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: fine.

articles.title: Carbon Weave (Spec)
articles.summary: Fine even woven crosshatch in the clearcoat; tight diagonal twill grid, low contrast, uniform sheen break-up. A smooth sheen with a very fine checkered grain; carbon-ish rather than a bold weave.
articles.what: Adds woven fiber crosshatch roughness pattern simulating carbon fiber surface texture on spec maps Up close: A fine square basket-weave grid, about 12 px per cell, visible as faint crosshatch lines in the lit band on metal and in the dark floor area; on satin it is just a trace of grain. Straight over-under crosshatch with no diagonal. From a distance: A smooth sheen with a very fine checkered grain; carbon-ish rather than a bold weave. It changes the shine only, never the colour. articles.title: Laser Etched
articles.summary: Sharp etched border strips break a polished tile into hard rough and oxidised bands, crisp step edges. Reads as a clean smooth sheen; any tile and border design would only appear across a whole panel.
articles.what: Laser-etched pattern on polished surface — sharp step-function boundary (FBM-wobbled edge) between etched border strips (G=200+ rough, R=40 oxidized) and polished tile ce Up close: Almost smooth: a very fine regular stipple of tiny dots about 10 px apart, visible only inside the highlight on metal. The etched border strips and polished tile cells in the description are far bigger than this crop and do not show here. From a distance: Reads as a clean smooth sheen; any tile and border design would only appear across a whole panel. It changes the shine only, never the colour. articles.title: PVD Coating
articles.summary: Ultra-fine metallic grain, near-mirror smooth with faint nodule sparkle. Reads as a smooth liquid-metal sheen with a slight rippled shimmer inside the highlight; the swirls fade into a soft glare.
articles.what: Physical Vapor Deposition nodule texture — ultra-fine Voronoi (80+ cells/unit) nucleation sites, very high metallic 180-240/255 throughout, near-zero roughness G: 10-30/2 Up close: Soft rippling interference swirls, small wavy loops and ovals about 10-20 px, like oil-slick or moire rings, stirred across the highlight. They are smooth, soft-edged and wavering, with no sharp cells. From a distance: Reads as a smooth liquid-metal sheen with a slight rippled shimmer inside the highlight; the swirls fade into a soft glare. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Surface & Spray Texture (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
